factorRatings.note: The Stranger (2011) and Seattle Weekly (2012) both describe a thin, Neapolitan-meets-NYC crust with big blackened bubbles at the edges, built up with quality ingredients like Mama Lil's peppers, Fra' Mani sausage, and chevre, and call it a dependable, kid-friendly neighborhood spot by the Madison Park beach despite cramped seating and slow service.

Seattle Met's 2019 South End roundup describes Breezy Town, the Clock-Out Lounge spinoff of Windy City Pie, baking deep-dish-style pies on a tangy sourdough crust that splits the difference between Chicago and Detroit styles, recommending the double-meat 'Pepperoni Paint Job' and praising its 'bizarre and wonderful' experimental specials.

The Stranger's 2014 review calls chef Mike Easton's weekday-lunch-only Roman-style pizza al taglio 'extremely good': a naturally fermented, focaccia-like crust re-baked to order after topping, sold by weight at $32/kg (a filling lunch under $10), with combinations like mortadella-pistachio-pesto and chanterelle-lobster-aioli that the writer says each topped the last.
